status.triage: Each status.* key: an issue's status on the team's issue tracker, shown on badges, board columns and menus. Short, title case where your language uses it. The first status: a new issue waiting for an admin to sort it (kind, priority, area).
status.open: Status: sorted and waiting for someone to start it (an adjective, not the verb).
status.ready: Status: ready for someone to work on.
status.in_progress: Status: someone is working on it.
status.in_review: Status: the work is done and waiting for review.
status.blocked: Status: work can't go on until something else is done.
status.wont_fix: The status of an issue closed without doing it.
priority.critical: Each priority.* key: an issue's priority, on a small colored pill.
kind.bug: Each kind.* key: what sort of issue it is (a bug, a feature request, documentation work…).
kind.feature: Kind: a request for something new.
kind.improvement: Kind: making something that exists better.
kind.chore: Kind: routine upkeep work (cleanup, upgrades) that users don't see.
kind.request: An issue a socio (an AI agent) filed to ask for a capability it lacks. "Socio" is a product noun.
area.server: Each area.* key: the part of the product an issue is about, shown on tags and in filters.
area.client: Area: the web app people use in the browser.
area.chat: The chat in the web app.
area.schedules: Area: scheduled tasks, jobs a socio (AI agent) runs at set times.
area.telegram: Area: talking to socios through Telegram. Telegram is a name; keep it.
area.model: The AI model the product runs on.
area.runs: Runs: each time a socio (AI agent) works on a turn.
area.spaces: "Spaces" is a product noun: shared folders of pages and data.
area.learning: Area: Learning, where socios (AI agents) learn procedures (skills) from the team's finished conversations.
area.computers: The virtual computers socios (AI agents) use.
label.owner-lead: Each label.* key: a fixed label on issues. The English keeps the stored form (lowercase, with a hyphen or colon); you may write it as words in your language. The work is owned by the lead agent, not by an app user.
label.owner-user: The work is owned by the person outside the app.
label.needs-decision: A person has to decide something before work goes on.
label.regression: Label: something that used to work broke.
label.performance: Label: about speed or resource use.
label.good-first-issue: A small issue suited to a newcomer.
label.dot-request: An issue a socio (AI agent) filed to ask for a capability.
tag.priority: Tooltip of a priority pill; {{priority}} is a priority's name (priority.*).
tag.kind: Tooltip of the tag that shows an issue's kind.
tag.area: Tooltip of the tag that shows an issue's area.
tag.label: Tooltip of a tag that shows one of an issue's labels.
ref: Tooltip and accessible name of a link to an issue: {{key}} is its key (CB-12), {{title}} its title.
component.all-plugins: A component (what an issue is about) that stands for every plugin. Plugins add pages and tools to the app.
component.all-apps: A component that stands for every mini app people publish in the workspace.
component.title: Tooltip of a component chip; {{name}} is the plugin's or app's name, {{owner}} the person who owns the app, {{note}} its state (component.state.*). The forms add the owner, the note, or both.
component.state.disabled: After a plugin's name: an admin turned the plugin off.
component.state.uninstalled: After a plugin's name: the plugin was removed.
component.state.deleted: After an app's name: the app was deleted.
component.note: A component's state in parentheses after its name; {{note}} is a component.state.* word.
